title: Sam Altman says OpenAI won’t go public until its models are safe
slides: Sam Altman ties IPO to AI safety first
But safety has no agreed definition
Founders can now delay investor exits indefinitely
thread_text:
1. OpenAI's IPO Paradox

Sam Altman says going public depends on AI safety – but safety has no agreed definition. So who really decides?

2. Altman's Safety Condition

He tied the IPO to safety first. That sounds noble, but it leaves the timing entirely in his hands.

3. Safety Is Undefined

No universal standard exists for 'safe AI'. Without a benchmark, 'safe enough' becomes a judgment call.

4. Founders Can Delay Exits

New structures let founders postpone investor payouts indefinitely. Altman's safety clause fits that playbook.

5. Who Decides Safe Enough?

Take a prompt on ChatGPT and ask it to define AI safety. Then ask yourself: would you trust that answer to time a trillion-dollar IPO?
video_script: Sam Altman says OpenAI will go public only when AI is safe.
But nobody agrees on what safe actually means.
So he gets to decide when it's safe enough.
New rules let founders delay investor payouts indefinitely.
Ask yourself: who should really decide?

Sam Altman said OpenAI won't go public until its models are "safe" — a condition with no agreed definition 🤔
